proposals.before: Yingshi especially faulted Master Zichang for arranging annals by year but writing biographical accounts instead, which later generations followed—this was not canonical teaching.
proposals.after: Yingshi especially faulted Master Zichang for not compiling year-by-year annals and writing biographical accounts instead, which later generations followed—this was not canonical teaching.
proposals.reason: Chinese 不編年而為列傳 means he did not use annalistic year-by-year form but wrote liezhuan biographies; the idiomatic English reverses this into arranging annals by year.

proposals.before: After the three schools of the Spring and Autumn, he recorded only those who had received instruction in Qi.
proposals.after: After the three schools of the Spring and Autumn, he recorded only what could instruct and regulate the living.
proposals.reason: 訓齊生人 means instruct and order the living people, not the polity Qi; the idiomatic reading invents a place name.

proposals.before: After the three schools of the Spring and Autumn, only those who received the instruction of Qi were recorded.
proposals.after: After the three schools of the Spring and Autumn, only what instructed and regulated the living was recorded.
proposals.reason: Same misreading of 訓齊生人 as instruction of Qi rather than the verb compound instruct-and-order the living.

proposals.before: Zheng and Ming were most renowned; Tan and Shi passed their fame down through literature.
proposals.after: Zheng and Chui were most renowned; Tan and Shi passed their fame down through literature.
proposals.reason: Literal 'Ming' invents a person; the idiomatic correctly pairs Zheng with Chui (垂 from s0064), matching the cohort summary.

proposals.before: Gao Shi recommended him for trial appointment as judge of the Grand Court and as investigation commissioner of Huainan.
proposals.after: Gao Shi recommended him for trial appointment as judge of the Grand Court and as administrative assistant to the investigation commissioner of Huainan.
proposals.reason: 淮南采訪判官 is the commissioner's assistant/judge (判官), not the investigation commissioner himself.

proposals.before: Gao Shi memorialized to try him as Judge of the Grand Court and as Investigation Commissioner of Huainan.
proposals.after: Gao Shi memorialized to try him as Judge of the Grand Court and as Administrative Assistant to the Investigation Commissioner of Huainan.
proposals.reason: Same office error: 判官 is not 采訪使.

proposals.before: Yan Zhenqing, military governor of Zhexi, recommended him as marching sima; he was summoned as attendant of the heir apparent but firmly declined.
proposals.after: Yan Zhenqing, military governor of Zhexi, recommended him as marching sima; he was summoned as Imperial Diarist but firmly declined.
proposals.reason: 起居舍人 is Imperial Diarist, not attendant of the heir apparent.

proposals.before: Yan Zhenqing, Military Governor of Zhexi, memorialized him as Marching Sima; he was summoned as Attendant of the Heir Apparent, but firmly declined.
proposals.after: Yan Zhenqing, Military Governor of Zhexi, memorialized him as Marching Sima; he was summoned as Imperial Diarist, but firmly declined.
proposals.reason: Same mistranslation of 起居舍人.

proposals.before: He died at forty-six; Hui and the others wore mourning and went weeping; an edict enfeoffed him as Vice Director of the Palace Library.
proposals.after: He died at forty-six; Hui and the others wore mourning and went weeping; an edict posthumously appointed him Vice Director of the Palace Library.
proposals.reason: 贈 is posthumous appointment, not enfeoffment.

proposals.before: A palace envoy passed through the province and demanded bribes without end; Wang Sui, magistrate of Nanchang, wished to prosecute him and sought Gao's counsel.
proposals.after: A palace envoy passed through the province and demanded bribes without end; Wang Gou, magistrate of Nanchang, wished to prosecute him and sought Gao's counsel.
proposals.reason: 王遘 is Wang Gou; 'Sui' misromanizes 遘.

proposals.before: A palace envoy passed through the province and sought gain without limit; Magistrate Wang Sui of Nanchang wished to prosecute him and consulted with Gao.
proposals.after: A palace envoy passed through the province and sought gain without limit; Magistrate Wang Gou of Nanchang wished to prosecute him and consulted with Gao.
proposals.reason: Same romanization error for 王遘.

proposals.before: Sui understood and thanked him profusely.
proposals.after: Gou understood and thanked him profusely.
proposals.reason: Short name must match 遘 as Gou.

proposals.before: Sui understood, and thanked him lavishly.
proposals.after: Gou understood, and thanked him lavishly.
proposals.reason: Short name must match 遘 as Gou.

proposals.before: When Lushan rebelled he sent Cai Xide with a sealed blade to summon him, saying: "If you still will not rise, cut off your head and bring it to me."
proposals.after: When Lushan rebelled he sent Cai Xide with a sealed blade to summon him, saying: "If he still will not rise, cut off his head and bring it to me."
proposals.reason: Chinese 斷其頭 is third-person 'his head' in the order to Cai about Ji; the literal wrongly switches to second-person 'your head'.

proposals.before: when the harvest was abundant he distributed the surplus among the poor and narrow-minded in the village.
proposals.after: when the harvest was abundant he distributed the surplus among the poor and straitened in the village.
proposals.reason: 貧狹 means the poor and hard-pressed, not 'narrow-minded'; the literal invents a moral judgment absent from the Chinese.

proposals.before: Emperor Suzong ordered him lodged in the offices of the Three Departments and had defiled officials bow in ranks to shame his heart.
proposals.after: Emperor Suzong ordered him lodged in the offices of the Three Departments and had defiled officials bow in ranks to shame their hearts.
proposals.reason: 以愧其心 refers to shaming the defiled officials (其), not Ji's heart; the literal misassigns the pronoun.

proposals.before: Lai Tian recruited him as staff officer for Xiangyang in Shanxi, and he was appointed vice director of the Ministry of Rites.
proposals.after: Lai Tian recruited him as staff officer for Xiangyang in Shaanxi, and he was appointed vice director of the Ministry of Rites.
proposals.reason: 陜西 denotes the Tang Shaanxi circuit, not Shanxi; the idiomatic place name is geographically wrong.

proposals.before: The next day twenty who came to Cheng to return home to care for parents; those who had not attended parents for three years he expelled.
proposals.after: The next day twenty came to Cheng to return home and care for their parents; those who had not attended their parents for three years he expelled.
proposals.reason: Literal English is ungrammatical and omits the finite verb for the twenty students who came to Cheng.

proposals.before: At the gates of Bian Que and Chunyu Yi they did not reject the sick;
proposals.after: At the gates of Yu Fu and Bian Que they did not reject the sick;
proposals.reason: 俞、扁 is the classical physician pair Yu Fu (俞跗) and Bian Que (扁鵲); Chunyu Yi misidentifies 俞 and reverses the Chinese order.

proposals.before: At the gates of Bian Que and Chunyu Yi they did not reject the sick;
proposals.after: At the gates of Yu Fu and Bian Que they did not reject the sick;
proposals.reason: Literal English should match 俞、扁 as Yu Fu then Bian Que, not Bian Que and Chunyu Yi.

proposals.before: Fortunate to live in an age without taboo, I cannot set forth the larger pattern; hearing that your office is sending Master Yang back south.
proposals.after: Fortunate to live in an age without taboo, I cannot set forth the larger pattern, nor inform your office, regarding Master Yang's being sent back south.
proposals.reason: Literal English is a sentence fragment and under-translates 不能論列大體，聞下執事，還陽公之南也.

proposals.before: The prefecture produced dwarfs who were sent yearly as tribute to court; Cheng grieved that they were torn from their lives and had nowhere to advance.
proposals.after: The prefecture produced dwarfs who were sent yearly as tribute to court; Cheng grieved that they were torn from home by separation, and he presented none.
proposals.reason: 無所進 means Cheng offered no dwarf tribute, not that the dwarfs had nowhere to advance; 生離 is separation from home while living.

proposals.before: At first, when Zhu Ci rebelled, the students were about to follow the rebellion; Fan sternly rebuked them and they would not listen, so none of the six halls' scholars were defiled.
proposals.after: At first, when Zhu Ci rebelled, the students were about to follow the rebellion; Fan sternly rebuked them until they desisted, so none of the six halls' scholars were defiled.
proposals.reason: 叱不聽 with the outcome that none were defiled means the students ceased following the rebels; 'would not listen' reverses the sense.

proposals.before: Ji Chang was from Lu.
proposals.after: Chang was from Lu.
proposals.reason: Chinese has only 償; the surname Ji is not in the source and is an invention.

proposals.before: Wang Luqing passed the jinshi and was renowned.
proposals.after: Lu Qing passed the jinshi and was renowned.
proposals.reason: Chinese has only 魯卿; the surname Wang is not in the source and is an invention.

proposals.before: When the court moved to Luoyang, Liu Can, hoping to please the wicked ministers, slaughtered the empire's talent to aid the ruined royal house; an edict summoned Tu to court; Tu pretended to drop his tablet and affected the manner of a rustic old man.
proposals.after: When the court moved to Luoyang, Liu Can, hoping to please the wicked ministers, slaughtered the empire's talent to help destroy the royal house; an edict summoned Tu to court; Tu pretended to drop his tablet and affected the manner of a rustic old man.
proposals.reason: 助喪王室 means helping bring about the ruin of the royal house, not aiding an already ruined house.

proposals.before: He built a plain pavilion and lodge, painting all the Tang's men of integrity and literary men; he named the pavilion Xiuxiu and wrote a text to show his aim: "Xiu means beautiful; once xiu, beauty is complete.
proposals.after: He built a plain pavilion and lodge, painting all the Tang's men of integrity and literary men; he named the pavilion Xiuxiu and wrote a text to show his aim: "Xiu means beautiful; once at rest, beauty is complete.
proposals.reason: Literal leaves the verb 休 untranslated as xiu after defining it; the sense is once at rest, matching the idiomatic rendering.

proposals.before: Dexiu by virtue, Cheng by blunt integrity, Tu by knowing fate—their aims contended with autumn frost in severity; true husbands indeed!
proposals.after: Dexiu by virtue, Cheng by blunt integrity, Tu by knowing fate—their aims contended with autumn frost in severity; true men indeed!
proposals.reason: 丈夫 here means upright men of character, not husbands; the idiomatic field already renders true men.

decisions.reason: 不編年而為列傳 means Zichang did not compile year-by-year annals but wrote biographies; the before text reverses the negation into arranging annals by year.
訓齊生人 is the verb compound “instruct and regulate the living,” not “instruction in Qi”; the before invents the polity name 齊.
Same error as the idiomatic field: 訓齊生人 means what instructs and regulates the living, not “the instruction of Qi.”

decisions.after: Zheng and E were most renowned; Tan and Shi passed their fame down through literature.
decisions.reason: Authoritative witnesses read 拯與崿名最著: the pair is Zheng and Li E (崿/㟧), not “Ming” from bare 名 and not Chui (垂). The chapter dossier omits 崿; Chui belongs to the earlier roster, not this summary.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 拯與崿名最著，潭、識以文傳後

decisions.reason: 淮南采訪判官 is administrative assistant/judge (判官) under the investigation commissioner, not the commissioner (采訪使) himself.
Same office error: 判官 is not 采訪使; the trial appointment is as Huainan investigation assistant.
起居舍人 is Imperial Diarist; attendant of the heir apparent would be 太子舍人, a different office.
Same mistranslation: 起居舍人 is Imperial Diarist, not Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
詔贈 is a posthumous appointment/grant, not enfeoffment.
王遘 is Wang Gou (Gòu); Sui misromanizes 遘.
Same romanization fix: 遘 is Gou, not Sui.
Short form 遘 must be Gou to match the personal name.
Same short-name fix: 遘 is Gou.
Lushan’s order to Cai about Ji uses 斷其頭 (his head) and third-person 即不起; second-person “your head” invents address to Ji.
貧狹 means the poor and hard-pressed, not “narrow-minded”; the before invents a moral judgment absent from the Chinese.
以愧其心 follows 使汙賊官羅拜: 其 refers to the defiled officials’ hearts, not Ji’s.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 使汙賊官羅拜，以愧其心

decisions.reason: 陜西 is the Tang Shaanxi circuit (west of the passes), not Shanxi (山西).
謁城還養者二十輩 needs a finite verb; the before is an ungrammatical fragment, and the repair matches the Chinese and the idiomatic.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 明日謁城還養者二十輩

decisions.reason: 俞、扁 is the classical physician pair Yu Fu (俞跗) then Bian Que (扁鵲); Chunyu Yi misidentifies 俞 and reverses the order.
Same identification: 俞、扁 are Yu Fu and Bian Que in that order, not Bian Que and Chunyu Yi.
不能論列大體，聞下執事 pairs “set forth the larger pattern” with “inform your office” about 還陽公之南; the before is a fragment and misreads 聞 as mere hearing.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 不能論列大體，聞下執事，還陽公之南也

decisions.reason: 生離 is living separation from home, and 無所進 means Cheng presented no dwarf tribute, not that the dwarfs had nowhere to advance.
With 故六館士無受汙者, 叱不聽 means Fan’s rebuke stopped them; “they would not listen” reverses the outcome.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 蕃正色叱不聽，故六館士無受汙者

decisions.reason: The same man is named 季償 earlier in this chapter among the students who petitioned for Cheng; “Ji Chang” is accurate chapter context, not an invention, so the before is accurate enough.
The same man is named 王魯卿 earlier in this chapter; “Wang Luqing” keeps that surname, while “Lu Qing” wrongly splits the given name and drops attested 王.
助喪王室 means helping bring about the ruin of the royal house; “aid the ruined royal house” misreads 喪 as an adjective.
After defining 休 as “beautiful,” 既休而美具 uses 休 as “at rest”; leaving it as untranslated “xiu” under-translates the verb.
丈夫 here praises upright men of character, not husbands; the idiomatic “true men” is the right sense.
